text: Writing f = u + iv with z = x + iy, the book states f is holomorphic precisely when u and v satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations, namely:
explanation: The Cauchy-Riemann equations ∂u/∂x = ∂v/∂y and ∂u/∂y = −∂v/∂x force the difference quotient defining f'(z) to agree from all directions in ℂ. The last option states that u and v are harmonic (∇²u = 0), which is a consequence of holomorphy, not the defining equations; the first has the signs reversed.
